look_here_first: Start with leaf size, bark, and ripe fruit: much larger leaves than Texas persimmon, dark blocky/checkered mature bark, and yellow-orange to reddish ripe fruit rather than black.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves much larger than Diospyros texana

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: larger yellow-orange to reddish ripe fruit

key_traits.label: Field comparison
key_traits.text: Mature bark deeply checkered/blackish; leaves normally larger (approx. 3.5–8 cm in USDA description) and often pointed; ripe berries yellowish-orange to reddish; calyx persists (often 4 broad lobes). Texas persimmon usually smaller blunt leaves and smooth gray bark with ripe black berry.

lookalikes.differences: D. texana has smaller thick leaves, pale smooth peeling bark, and black fruit.
